rule: A case is in this release only if the Astra review status is approved.
note: One model review of synthetic scoring keys. Not a physician panel, not a confirmed clinical label, and not medical advice.

cases.label: DLB
cases.comment: With CDR 1, CDR-SB 4.5, hallucinations, parkinsonism and executive impairment, a 1.5-point two-year increase with decline=true is a plausible modest trajectory. The saved model predicts +4.0 with decline=true (reward 0.650); that is also plausible, but not demonstrably more sensible than the gold from this single note, and its asserted annual rate is unsupported here. Approval is of plausibility, not of a uniquely predictable number; the rubric does not evaluate the forecast magnitude.

flagged_criteria.comment: The saved judge marked this met, but the response does not say that no specific LATE test was available in the cited consensus, as the affirmative second sentence requires; merely avoiding an invented cutoff does not satisfy the whole item.

cases.label: DLB
cases.comment: CDR 1/CDR-SB 7.5 with gradual memory decline, parkinsonism and active sleep makes a 4.5-point two-year increase plausible, although relatively brisk. The vignette does not establish an individual rate; this approves the trajectory as a reasonable possibility and decline=true at the bench threshold, not the hidden DLB label.

cases.label: AD
cases.comment: Visible CSF Aβ42 732 is below 1100, p-tau181 40.2 exceeds 24, tau PET 1.61 exceeds 1.23, and t-tau 400 exceeds 235, supporting A+/T+/N+ under the bench rules.

cases.label: DLB
cases.comment: Dementia with fluctuations, formed visual hallucinations and parkinsonism supports the DLB-dominant vector (84%); a stepwise course supports retaining a vascular alternative. The negative visible amyloid/tau markers fit low AD probability; no exact probability calibration is implied.

cases.label: AD
cases.comment: Gradual amnestic impairment at CDR 1/CDR-SB 4.5 with positive amyloid and tau markers makes +1.5 points over two years and decline=true a plausible modest trajectory. White-matter disease adds uncertainty to the rate but does not make this proposed increase implausible.

cases.label: mixed
cases.comment: CDR-SB 17.5 leaves only 0.5 points before the scale maximum, so a zero recorded increase and decline=false are fair ceiling-limited targets. Here decline means an increase of at least 1 point in the generator, not absence of clinical deterioration; the hidden mixed label is not being endorsed.

cases.label: vascular
cases.comment: Stepwise decline, executive impairment, mild cognitive deficits and extensive white-matter hyperintensities support a vascular-dominant differential (78%). The isolated hallucination warrants an alternative, but does not outweigh the vascular pattern; the negative AD markers support low AD probability.

cases.label: AD
cases.comment: At CDR-SB 18 the scale cannot increase, so +0.0 and decline=false are correct for the bench's measured-change definition. This ceiling effect must not be read as clinical stability in the severely impaired synthetic presentation.

cases.label: AD
cases.comment: Gradual memory decline at CDR 1 with MMSE 23/MoCA 21 and positive CSF amyloid/tau supports +2.5 points over two years with decline=true as a plausible trajectory. The missing baseline CDR-SB limits precision, but the visible stage leaves room for this amount of worsening.

cases.label: AD
cases.comment: Gradual amnestic dementia with CSF Aβ42 655, amyloid PET 53.8 and tau PET 1.72 supports an AD-dominant distribution (86%). A hallucination alone does not establish DLB; retaining mixed pathology as an alternative is reasonable.

cases.label: AD
cases.comment: Moderate impairment at CDR 2/CDR-SB 14.5 with concordantly positive CSF amyloid/tau supports a +2.5-point trajectory that remains below the scale ceiling. The sparse symptom history limits etiologic detail but does not contradict decline=true over two years.

cases.label: FTLD-TDP
cases.comment: CDR-SB 0, MMSE 28 and MoCA 27 without a documented progressive course make a stable recorded two-year CDR-SB trajectory a defensible conservative target. Behavior/language change and posterior atrophy warrant uncertainty and follow-up; approval of +0.0/decline=false does not endorse the hidden FTLD-TDP label or guarantee stability.

cases.label: FTLD-TDP
cases.comment: Visible Aβ42 1491 and amyloid PET 11.3 are negative, p-tau181 15.4 is negative, and t-tau 176 is below the N cutoff, matching A-/T-/N-. N-negative is the bench's t-tau call, not a denial of the posterior atrophy described on MRI.

cases.label: vascular
cases.comment: Stepwise cognitive decline with executive impairment and no structural imaging shown makes mri_brain a fair next test to assess a possible vascular contribution. This is supported by the visible note rather than merely by the hidden vascular label.

cases.label: FTLD-TDP
cases.comment: Gradual behavioral change with CDR 2/CDR-SB 11, impaired screens and asymmetric atrophy supports a plausible +2.5-point increase with decline=true. The trajectory does not require accepting the unconfirmed FTLD-TDP protein label.

cases.label: DLB
cases.comment: Dementia at CDR 1 with fluctuations and parkinsonism supports a DLB-dominant vector (82%), while the displayed plasma/tau PET results do not support AD. Motor-versus-cognitive onset timing is missing, so this remains a differential rather than a confirmed DLB diagnosis.

cases.label: FTLD-tau
cases.comment: With CDR 3/CDR-SB 16, severe test impairment and frontal atrophy, a +1-point two-year change is plausible and fits the limited remaining scale range. The stepwise course leaves etiology uncertain, but does not make this modest worsening or decline=true unfair.

cases.label: AD
cases.comment: Visible Aβ42 606/amyloid PET 71.9, p-tau181 40.0 and t-tau 493 cross their respective bench thresholds, supporting A+/T+/N+.

cases.label: AD
cases.comment: Marked cognitive impairment and worsening memory with amyloid PET 73.6 and elevated p-tau181/plasma p-tau217 support AD as the mode. The substantial mixed probability is reasonable uncertainty at age 95; the chart does not confirm a specific second pathology.

cases.label: FTLD-TDP
cases.comment: Gradual multidomain decline with CDR 2/MoCA 10 and posterior atrophy makes +3 points and decline=true a plausible two-year trajectory. The missing baseline CDR-SB limits precision, and the hidden FTLD-TDP assignment is not needed or endorsed for this T2 judgment.

cases.label: vascular
cases.comment: CSF Aβ42 1514, p-tau181 10.4 and t-tau 150 support A-/T-/N- using the stated thresholds. Frontal atrophy and severe impairment do not change the generator's operational t-tau N call; they do preclude interpreting N-negative as absence of brain disease.

cases.label: DLB
cases.comment: At CDR-SB 17.5 only a 0.5-point increase is possible, so +0.5 and decline=false match the scale ceiling and the generator's at-least-1-point decline threshold. This does not mean no clinical deterioration in the severe fluctuating/parkinsonian presentation.

cases.label: FTLD-TDP
cases.comment: Visible Aβ42 1443, p-tau181 14.8/tau PET 1.06 and t-tau 144 support A-/T-/N- under the bench cutoffs. Severe impairment does not itself reverse any of these measurement-based calls.

cases.label: DLB
cases.comment: Fluctuations and parkinsonism with active sleep support considering Lewy-body disease, while extensive white-matter disease leaves an etiologic alternative that DAT imaging could help assess. No DAT result is already shown, so datscan is a defensible next test within the closed list, although utility at this severe stage would depend on an unstated decision.

cases.label: AD
cases.comment: CDR-SB 17.5 limits worsening to 0.5 points, so +0.5/decline=false is consistent with the bench definition despite severe impairment and positive AD markers. The boolean must not be interpreted as clinical stability.

cases.label: mixed
cases.comment: Visible Aβ42 1494/amyloid PET 1.5 and p-tau181 15.4/tau PET 1.08 are negative, while t-tau 449 exceeds 235, matching A-/T-/N+. The mild or normal screening scores do not negate the measurement-based N call.

cases.label: FTLD-tau
cases.comment: Normal MMSE/MoCA 29 and CDR-SB 0 make a small +0.5-point change below the bench decline threshold a plausible conservative two-year trajectory. Reported cognitive symptoms and asymmetric atrophy warrant uncertainty; the forecast is not proof of stability or of the hidden FTLD-tau label.

cases.label: AD
cases.comment: Progressive amnestic dementia with CSF Aβ42 688 and p-tau181 41.4 supports the AD mode, while parkinsonism and frontal atrophy justify keeping mixed pathology in the differential. The high mixed probability is uncertain and does not identify a second pathology, but the broad AD-versus-mixed allocation is defensible as a differential rather than a precise calibrated estimate.

cases.label: AD
cases.comment: Gradual memory decline, CDR 2/CDR-SB 14 and positive amyloid markers make +1.5 points over two years with decline=true a plausible modest trajectory. The projected score remains within the scale and the note does not support a uniquely precise rate.
